reviewer.affiliation: OpenAI Codex, commissioned by the Wirestack repository owner
reviewer.independenceStatement: I received a frozen source snapshot, the asserted candidate commit, preserved audit material, and orchestrator-provided remote-state evidence. I had no implementation role, inherited no implementation discussion, made no product or test changes, and reached dispositions from source, report bytes, and bounded validation.
conflicts: The process-isolated Codex verifier was commissioned by the same repository owner through the implementation orchestrator.
Process isolation does not provide the organizational independence of an external security firm.
Remote GitHub state was supplied by the orchestrator and was not independently queried by this verifier.

findings.title: Canonical TLS provider manifest was missing
findings.reproduction: Start a standard CJPM lifecycle from a checkout that contains only repository inputs.
findings.impact: The old tree could not reproduce its provider build without an untracked manifest.
findings.evidence: The candidate has the exact AWS-LC 5.5.0 commit manifest, the build tool validates it, and hosted clean-checkout evidence reports a successful provider and current-source build.
findings.fix: Track and validate the canonical AWS-LC manifest as a release input.

regressions.command: python3 -m unittest focused M7-029 build, release, and supply-chain contracts -v

findings.dispositionRationale: Tracked input, static contract, and hosted clean-checkout execution close the missing-input failure.

findings.title: Pull requests lacked a required clean Cangjie gate
findings.reproduction: Inspect the pull-request workflow and main ruleset, then observe the clean hosted job on the candidate.
findings.impact: Broken native inputs or Cangjie sources could previously merge behind green partial checks.
findings.evidence: The workflow uses a clean hosted checkout and runs repository readiness, current-source architecture/build/test, installed consumer, and mutation checks. Committed evidence records successful run 33233671568 and strict ruleset 21787899. Orchestrator-provided remote-final-state.json separately reports successful run 33237855698 on exact candidate ea493f13fefa520e9c1f2e08b9b068dc26c28082 and the same active strict ruleset.
findings.fix: Add the canonical hosted clean build and enforce clean-cangjie-build on main with no bypass actors.
findings.dispositionRationale: Repository workflow, executed hosted check, and enforced strict status context now satisfy the original merge-gate property.

findings.title: CJPM hook omitted the resolver archive
findings.reproduction: Run cjpm check with resolver output absent.
findings.impact: A clean lifecycle could fail after building only TLS native inputs.
findings.evidence: Every CJPM phase calls the combined native builder and the missing-resolver reproduction completes cjpm check.
findings.fix: Build provider and resolver inputs from one pre-phase hook.

regressions.command: codex_cangjie_env cjpm check with target/native/resolver absent

findings.dispositionRationale: The exact prior failure precondition now succeeds.

findings.title: Qualification freshness omitted native and build inputs
findings.reproduction: Mutate a provider or resolver manifest, native source, build script, lockfile, or build hook and validate old qualification.
findings.impact: Old release evidence could remain current after a native or build-control change.
findings.evidence: M7-021 now binds native manifests, C and header sources, build tools, build.cj, lockfile, and manifest; focused mutation tests pass.
findings.fix: Expand qualification inputs to every release-critical native and build control.

regressions.command: python3 -m unittest focused M7-029 build, release, and supply-chain contracts -v

findings.dispositionRationale: Input drift now invalidates old qualification. Current candidate regeneration remains a separate Medium release-evidence issue.

findings.title: Main lacked required checks and protection
findings.reproduction: Query repository rulesets and default-branch protection.
findings.impact: Security controls could previously be bypassed by direct or non-fast-forward updates.
findings.evidence: Committed and orchestrator-provided remote evidence report active ruleset 21787899, strict clean-cangjie-build, deletion and non-fast-forward prohibitions, no bypass actors, and current_user_can_bypass never.
findings.fix: Activate a strict main ruleset requiring the clean hosted gate.
findings.dispositionRationale: The required context and update protections are active with no bypass actor.

findings.title: Server consumed DATA credit before queue admission
findings.reproduction: Force reserved DATA enqueue to fail and inspect stream and connection credit.
findings.impact: Failed admission could starve sibling streams.
findings.evidence: The event transfers its reservation through enqueueReservedData, which cancels on failure; ten scheduler cases pass.
findings.fix: Transfer the permit atomically to the writer.
findings.dispositionRationale: Ownership and failure cleanup are now one writer operation.

findings.title: Peer defaults and local SETTINGS were conflated
findings.reproduction: Start with non-RFC local receive limits and inspect initial peer state and SETTINGS.
findings.impact: Peers could disagree on frame, window, table, or stream limits.
findings.evidence: RFC peer defaults, local caps, and advertised settings are separate; nine focused cases pass.
findings.fix: Separate settings roles and advertise every finite non-default receive limit.
findings.dispositionRationale: State and wire advertisement now match RFC roles.

findings.title: Cancellation wrapper changed H2 completion semantics
findings.reproduction: Read declared length before delayed H2 END_STREAM or trailers through the public wrapper.
findings.impact: The wrapper could detach cancellation and complete too early.
findings.evidence: The wrapper preserves completesAtDeclaredLength and fourteen facade cases pass.
findings.dispositionRationale: Protocol EOF remains the completion event for wrapped H2 bodies.

findings.title: Release lacked a project license grant
findings.reproduction: Inspect root licensing files, payload, and SPDX metadata.
findings.impact: Downstream use and redistribution rights were unclear.
findings.evidence: Apache-2.0 LICENSE, AWS-LC notices, payload inventory, and SPDX license tests are present and pass.
findings.fix: Ship the project grant and exact third-party notices and bind them into metadata.

regressions.command: python3 -m unittest focused release license and SBOM tests -v

findings.dispositionRationale: The source and release contracts now carry an explicit grant and attribution.

findings.title: CONNECT pooling omitted proxy credential identity
findings.reproduction: Use rotated dynamic proxy credentials for the same proxy and origin.
findings.impact: A tunnel authenticated as one principal could serve another.
findings.evidence: Dynamic authenticated CONNECT tunnels are single lease and two proxy cases pass.
findings.fix: Fail closed to no reuse when no stable credential partition exists.
findings.dispositionRationale: Rotated credentials cannot share an authenticated tunnel.

findings.title: Blocked getaddrinfo could make resolver teardown and quarantine unbounded
findings.reproduction: Block one native lookup in each of eight one-worker pools, release public handles, attempt a ninth pool, then release the blocked calls and retry admission.
findings.impact: Without a process cap, repeated closed pools could retain unbounded workers and memory behind libc or NSS.
findings.evidence: Capacity reservation allows at most eight live pools and 64 workers. Close stops admission without joining blocked calls. The ninth create returns OVERLOADED with a zero handle. The committed native probe then releases all calls and observes a new pool admitted after reaping. The committed gate report is PASS and binds the probe binary. A fresh rerun in this snapshot could not complete the Cangjie portion because the provider fetch had no DNS, but its native global-bound subprobe independently returned PASS; that overall fresh gate is not counted as PASS.
findings.fix: Reserve process-wide pool and worker capacity before thread creation, quarantine stuck pools under detached reapers, fail closed at the cap, and return capacity only after safe reaping.
findings.dispositionRationale: The uninterruptible call remains quarantined, but total quarantined pools and workers are now bounded process-wide; overload and later recovery are both exercised.

findings.title: Ambiguous physical write timeout was retryable
findings.reproduction: Inject a timeout after entering the physical write without zero-byte commit proof.
findings.impact: Automatic retry could duplicate a request.
findings.evidence: Write timeout uses Never retryability and nineteen transport cases pass.
findings.fix: Treat unknown physical commit state as non-retryable.
findings.dispositionRationale: The default cannot resend an ambiguously committed write.

findings.title: Cancelling one accept closed the listener
findings.reproduction: Cancel one pending accept, then accept a later connection on the same listener.
findings.impact: One request could terminate the service listener.
findings.evidence: Accept uses operation-scoped bounded waits and the transport suite proves listener reuse.
findings.fix: Separate operation cancellation from listener lifetime.
findings.dispositionRationale: Only explicit close now terminates the listener.

findings.title: Trust changes did not alter TLS session partition
findings.reproduction: Replace a same-size bundle or modify hashed-directory certificates and compare source identity.
findings.impact: Old sessions could be offered after trust replacement.
findings.evidence: Bounded deterministic SHA-256 content identities cover bundle and directory entries; five adapter cases pass.
findings.fix: Bind the session trust identity to selected trust-store contents.
findings.dispositionRationale: Trust replacement changes the session partition.

findings.title: Role-invalid SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH was accepted
findings.reproduction: As a client, receive SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH from a server.
findings.impact: Role-invalid peer state could be accepted.
findings.evidence: Endpoint role is explicit and the settings regression exercises rejection.
findings.fix: Reject prohibited setting direction with PROTOCOL_ERROR.
findings.dispositionRationale: Role validation now fails closed.

findings.title: Resolver polled every pending job at one millisecond
findings.reproduction: Keep a native job pending through repeated polls and record waits.
findings.impact: Many slow lookups amplified scheduler wakeups.
findings.evidence: Waits now back off 1, 2, 4, 8, then 16 ms and stay capped; the committed resolver gate passes nine focused cases.
findings.fix: Use bounded exponential polling backoff under the canonical deadline.
findings.dispositionRationale: Pending polling is capped and no second timeout owner was added.

findings.title: Resolver FFI accepted unknown address-family values
findings.reproduction: Inject a native family other than explicit IPv4 or IPv6.
findings.impact: ABI drift or corruption could publish misclassified addresses.
findings.evidence: The decoder matches only family 4 or 6 and the committed focused gate includes the fail-closed family test.
findings.fix: Reject unknown native family as a typed system failure.
findings.dispositionRationale: Unknown ABI values no longer become addresses.

findings.title: ByteSpan exposes mutable backing storage
findings.reproduction: Mutate the original array or public bytes member while a ByteSpan exists.
findings.impact: The documented immutable-view property is not enforced.
findings.evidence: Array storage remains publicly writable.
findings.dispositionRationale: Open and unchanged.

findings.title: Historical public aliases targeted internal types
findings.reproduction: Inspect the current public alias target inventory.
findings.impact: Internal package identity would become public if any such alias remained.
findings.evidence: ADR-0006 intentionally replaced the pre-1.0 contract and the current M7-032 inventory reports zero internal alias targets.
findings.dispositionRationale: The reviewed candidate uses the replacement pre-1.0 public contract; compatibility with the old experimental aliases is explicitly non-gating.

findings.title: Cancellation callback registry has no hard bound
findings.reproduction: Register callbacks repeatedly on one live token without closing handles.
findings.impact: A public registry can grow without an explicit maximum.
findings.evidence: Callbacks remain in a HashMap with no configured admission cap.
findings.dispositionRationale: Open and unchanged.

findings.title: Other workflows retain mutable action tags
findings.reproduction: Inspect every workflow uses entry.
findings.impact: Non-canonical workflow dependencies can change without a repository commit.
findings.evidence: The clean release-critical workflow is pinned, but several other workflows still use major-version action tags.
findings.dispositionRationale: Residual risk is outside the required clean gate but remains open.

findings.title: Inbound HTTP/2 buffering lacks an independent byte cap
findings.reproduction: Queue maximum-sized DATA segments without consuming them.
findings.impact: Inbound memory policy is coupled to outbound segment count.
findings.evidence: Body-channel maxSegments still derives from maxPendingWrites and has no separate byte ceiling.
findings.dispositionRationale: Open and unchanged.

findings.title: Accepted IPv6 URL literals remain unusable in direct client factories
findings.reproduction: Parse a bracketed IPv6 URL and execute the client pipeline.
findings.impact: The parser accepts an origin the connector path cannot represent as HostName.
findings.evidence: Factories still route the colon-containing origin through HostName.
findings.dispositionRationale: Open and unchanged.

findings.title: Private-key metadata check and read are separate path operations
findings.reproduction: Replace or redirect the key path between metadata validation and read.
findings.impact: The loaded key can differ from the object whose metadata was checked.
findings.evidence: No same-handle no-follow read contract is present.
findings.dispositionRationale: Open and unchanged.

findings.title: TLS context key lifetime remains caller-controlled
findings.reproduction: Build a context, close the caller key reference, then handshake.
findings.impact: A built shared context can fail because the caller closes retained state.
findings.evidence: Context construction retains the same closeable reference without an independent lease.
findings.dispositionRationale: Open and unchanged.

findings.title: Candidate release qualification remains stale after public-contract remediation
findings.reproduction: Inspect evidence-index states for installation, performance, SBOM, provider manifest, and fingerprint.
findings.impact: This security-task candidate is not itself a fully qualified release candidate.
findings.evidence: Seven package entries remain STALE_AFTER_M7_032 and the 86,400-second final soak is still blocked.
findings.dispositionRationale: Open as a later release qualification issue; it does not reopen a High or Critical M7-029 finding.
